/**
 * The typewriter family. [textReveal] drives the real per-glyph reveal on a text
 * renderer; the fade + Wipe mask are only fallbacks for surfaces that can't do that
 * (curved text, media layers, the native export canvas).
 */
private fun typewriterVisualState(
    progress: Float,
    mode: TextRevealMode,
    durationMs: Long
): LayerAnimationVisualState = LayerAnimationVisualState(
    alphaMultiplier = (0.12f + progress * 0.88f).coerceIn(0f, 1f),
    revealMask = LayerRevealMaskSpec.Wipe(progress = progress),
    textReveal = TextRevealSpec(progress, mode, durationMs)
)

canva.source: docs/canva-animation-parity.md (web dashboard) — Canva's own tween builders
canva.repeating:
// ---- Repeating effects (§4, §8.3), one cycle = one `durationMs` ---------------------------------

/**
 * FLICKER (Canva's `owf`): opacity 1 → b over `a`, hold b for 200ms, b → 1 over `a` (LINEAR), with
 * `b = lerp(.6, .1, t)` and `a = max(0, (cycle − 200) / 2)`. [t] is Canva's `(Vd + 1) / 2`, which
 * the slot carries as `clamp(intensity − .5, 0, 1)` (a stacked flicker as `stackFlickerT`); the
 * picker's intensity 1 is Canva's default t = .5 (b = .35).
 */
internal fun canvaFlickerOpacity(cycleProgress: Float, cycleMs: Double, t: Double): Float {
    val cycle = max(1.0, cycleMs)
    val b = canvaLerpD(0.6, 0.1, t)
    val a = max(0.0, (cycle - CANVA_FLICKER_HOLD_MS) / 2.0)
    val ms = canvaExactProgress(cycleProgress) * cycle
    val dim = CanvaTween(delay = 0.0, duration = a, from = 1.0, to = b)
    val recover = CanvaTween(delay = a + CANVA_FLICKER_HOLD_MS, duration = a, from = b, to = 1.0)
    return (if (ms >= recover.delay) recover.valueAt(ms) else dim.valueAt(ms)).toFloat()
}

/**
 * PULSE: scale 1 → 1.15 over `q` (LINEAR), 1.15 → .85 over `a` (easeOutQuad), .85 → 1 over `q`
 * (LINEAR) with `q = a / 4`, so the cycle splits 1/6 : 2/3 : 1/6 whatever its length.
 */
internal fun canvaPulseScale(cycleProgress: Float): Float {
    val c = cycleProgress.coerceIn(0f, 1f)
    return when {
        c < 1f / 6f -> canvaLerp(1f, 1.15f, c * 6f)
        c < 5f / 6f -> canvaLerp(1.15f, 0.85f, canvaEaseOutQuad((c - 1f / 6f) * 1.5f))
        else -> canvaLerp(0.85f, 1f, (c - 5f / 6f) * 6f)
    }
}

internal data class CanvaWigglePose(val translationX: Float, val translationY: Float, val rotationDegrees: Float)

/**
 * WIGGLE, Canva's `rwf` step for step: `n = floor(lerp(10, 100, t))` steps of `g = cycle / (n + 1)`
 * with amplitude `lerp(.5, 1.8, t)`. Step i tweens the translation to
 * `(lerp(−20, 20, r(i + 2)), lerp(−20, 20, r(i + 3))) · amp` over g from `g·i` (easeInOutQuad), and —
 * for every step but the last — the rotation to `lerp(−10, 15, r(i + 1)) · amp` over g from
 * `g/2 + g·i`; after the n steps one more tween returns everything to 0 from `g·n`. Evaluated with
 * the latest-started-tween rule, so between rotation tweens the previous one's end holds. [t] is
 * `clamp(intensity − .5, 0, 1)` (default .5 → 55 steps of 325ms over 18.2s); `r` is
 * [canvaWiggleRandom] of the importer's `seed`, or of the layer size without one.
 */
internal fun canvaWigglePose(
    cycleProgress: Float,
    cycleMs: Double,
    t: Double,
    seed: Double?,
    width: Float,
    height: Float
): CanvaWigglePose {
    val n = floor(canvaLerpD(10.0, 100.0, t)).toInt()
    val amp = canvaLerpD(0.5, 1.8, t)
    val cycle = max(1.0, cycleMs)
    val g = cycle / (n + 1)
    val tau = canvaExactProgress(cycleProgress) * cycle
    fun r(step: Int) = canvaWiggleRandom(step, seed, width, height)
    fun targetX(i: Int) = canvaLerpD(-20.0, 20.0, r(i + 2)) * amp
    fun targetY(i: Int) = canvaLerpD(-20.0, 20.0, r(i + 3)) * amp
    fun targetRotation(i: Int) = canvaLerpD(-10.0, 15.0, r(i + 1)) * amp

    // Translation: step i (0 until n) at g·i, then the return at g·n — the latest started wins.
    var step = n
    while (step > 0 && tau < g * step) step--
    val fromX = if (step == 0) 0.0 else targetX(step - 1)
    val fromY = if (step == 0) 0.0 else targetY(step - 1)
    val toX = if (step == n) 0.0 else targetX(step)
    val toY = if (step == n) 0.0 else targetY(step)
    val x = CanvaTween(g * step, g, fromX, toX, CANVA_EASE_IN_OUT_QUAD).valueAt(tau)
    val y = CanvaTween(g * step, g, fromY, toY, CANVA_EASE_IN_OUT_QUAD).valueAt(tau)

    // Rotation: tweens j = 0 .. n − 2 at g/2 + g·j (the last step has none), then the return at g·n.
    val rotation = if (tau >= g * n) {
        CanvaTween(g * n, g, if (n >= 2) targetRotation(n - 2) else 0.0, 0.0, CANVA_EASE_IN_OUT_QUAD).valueAt(tau)
    } else {
        var j = n - 2
        while (j > 0 && tau < g / 2 + g * j) j--
        CanvaTween(
            g / 2 + g * j,
            g,
            if (j == 0) 0.0 else targetRotation(j - 1),
            targetRotation(j),
            CANVA_EASE_IN_OUT_QUAD
        ).valueAt(tau)
    }
    return CanvaWigglePose(x.toFloat(), y.toFloat(), rotation.toFloat())
}
canva.composition:
/*
 * Canva runs its continuous presets and repeating effects ALONGSIDE the entrance and exit, not
 * after them (docs/canva-animation-parity.md §8.2 in the web dashboard). A loop slot the importer
 * marks `concurrent` is attached to the playback state by the timeline resolver and composed here,
 * inside [resolveLayerAnimationVisualState], so every renderer call site stays unchanged.
 */

/**
 * Canva's `$pf` combine: alpha and the scales MULTIPLY, translation, rotation and blur ADD. The
 * structural channels (reveal mask, overlay bar, glyph motion, text reveal) stay this state's —
 * only the primary (entrance → hold → exit) state ever carries them.
 */
internal fun LayerAnimationVisualState.composedWith(other: LayerAnimationVisualState): LayerAnimationVisualState = copy(
    scaleMultiplier = scaleMultiplier * other.scaleMultiplier,
    scaleXMultiplier = scaleXMultiplier * other.scaleXMultiplier,
    scaleYMultiplier = scaleYMultiplier * other.scaleYMultiplier,
    rotationDeltaDegrees = rotationDeltaDegrees + other.rotationDeltaDegrees,
    translationX = translationX + other.translationX,
    translationY = translationY + other.translationY,
    alphaMultiplier = alphaMultiplier * other.alphaMultiplier,
    blurRadiusPx = blurRadiusPx + other.blurRadiusPx
)

/**
 * [primary] with the concurrent [loop] (and the stack it carries) composed on top.
 *
 * * Loop clock τ = [windowLocalMs] + `phaseMs`; with ramp params BREATHE/DRIFT/TECTONIC read
 *   [canvaContinuousRampVisual], anything else plays its LOOP formula at `(τ mod durationMs) /
 *   durationMs`.
 * * Stack: every `stack*` key plays its repeating effect at τs = [windowLocalMs] + `stackPhaseMs`
 *   on its own cycle.
 * * When the primary draws per writing-style unit (its [GlyphMotionSpec.canva] is set), what the
 *   LAYER keeps once a text renderer takes over alpha/blur/scale per unit is exactly the loop and
 *   stack contribution — stored on the spec as its rest values.
 */
internal fun composeCanvaConcurrentLoop(
    primary: LayerAnimationVisualState,
    loop: LayerAnimationSpec,
    windowLocalMs: Long,
    width: Float,
    height: Float,
    layerIndex: Int
): LayerAnimationVisualState {
    val tau = windowLocalMs.toDouble() + (loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.PHASE_MS) ?: 0.0)
    var rest = canvaConcurrentLoopVisual(loop, tau, width, height, layerIndex)
    val stackTau = windowLocalMs.toDouble() + (loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_PHASE_MS) ?: 0.0)
    canvaStackedEffects(loop, stackTau, width, height).forEach { rest = rest.composedWith(it) }
    val composed = primary.composedWith(rest)
    val glyph = primary.glyphMotion
    val canva = glyph?.canva ?: return composed
    return composed.copy(
        glyphMotion = glyph.copy(
            canva = canva.copy(
                restAlpha = rest.alphaMultiplier,
                restScale = rest.scaleMultiplier,
                restBlurPx = rest.blurRadiusPx
            )
        )
    )
}

/** The concurrent loop on its own at loop time [tau]. */
internal fun canvaConcurrentLoopVisual(
    loop: LayerAnimationSpec,
    tau: Double,
    width: Float,
    height: Float,
    layerIndex: Int
): LayerAnimationVisualState {
    canvaContinuousRampVisual(loop, tau)?.let { return it }
    val cycle = loop.durationMs.coerceAtLeast(1L).toDouble()
    val progress = (canvaFloorMod(tau, cycle) / cycle).toFloat().coerceIn(0f, 1f)
    return resolvePrimaryLayerAnimationVisualState(
        LayerTimelinePlaybackState(
            isVisible = true,
            localMs = canvaFloorMod(tau, cycle).toLong(),
            progress = progress,
            animation = loop.copy(infinite = true)
        ),
        width,
        height,
        layerIndex
    )
}

/**
 * BREATHE / DRIFT / TECTONIC with the importer's time-based ramp (r1…, optionally r2…), or null
 * when the loop carries none. BREATHE ramps the scale (and the y drift from y1…/y2…), DRIFT the
 * translation along its axis (UP/DOWN → y, otherwise x), TECTONIC the x translation.
 */
internal fun canvaContinuousRampVisual(loop: LayerAnimationSpec, tau: Double): LayerAnimationVisualState? {
    when (loop.type) {
        LayerAnimationType.BREATHE, LayerAnimationType.DRIFT, LayerAnimationType.TECTONIC -> Unit
        else -> return null
    }
    val to1 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R1_TO) ?: return null
    val from1 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R1_FROM) ?: to1
    val start1 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R1_START) ?: 0.0
    val dur1 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R1_DUR) ?: 0.0
    val ease1 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R1_EASE)?.toInt() ?: CANVA_EASE_LINEAR
    val twoSegment = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R2_DUR) != null
    val to2 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R2_TO) ?: to1
    val start2 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R2_START) ?: 0.0
    val dur2 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R2_DUR) ?: 0.0
    val ease2 = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.R2_EASE)?.toInt() ?: CANVA_EASE_LINEAR
    fun ramp(from: Double, to: Double, second: Double) =
        canvaRampValue(tau, from, to, start1, dur1, ease1, twoSegment, second, start2, dur2, ease2)

    val value = ramp(from1, to1, to2).toFloat()
    return when (loop.type) {
        LayerAnimationType.BREATHE -> {
            val y1To = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.Y1_TO)
            val y1From = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.Y1_FROM)
            val drift = if (y1To == null && y1From == null) {
                0f
            } else {
                val to = y1To ?: 0.0
                ramp(y1From ?: 0.0, to, loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.Y2_TO) ?: to).toFloat()
            }
            LayerAnimationVisualState(scaleMultiplier = value, translationY = drift)
        }
        LayerAnimationType.DRIFT -> when (loop.direction) {
            LayerAnimationDirection.UP, LayerAnimationDirection.DOWN -> LayerAnimationVisualState(translationY = value)
            else -> LayerAnimationVisualState(translationX = value)
        }
        else -> LayerAnimationVisualState(translationX = value)
    }
}

/**
 * The repeating effects stacked on a loop slot (`stackRotate` / `stackFlicker` / `stackPulse` /
 * `stackWiggle`, each valued in cycle ms) at stack time [tau]. A stacked ROTATE turns clockwise
 * unless its cycle is negative; FLICKER/WIGGLE take their `t` from `stackFlickerT` /
 * `stackWiggleT` (Canva's default 0.5 when absent); a stacked WIGGLE hashes the loop's `seed`.
 */
internal fun canvaStackedEffects(
    loop: LayerAnimationSpec,
    tau: Double,
    width: Float,
    height: Float
): List<LayerAnimationVisualState> {
    val effects = ArrayList<LayerAnimationVisualState>(4)
    fun progressOf(cycle: Double): Float = (canvaFloorMod(tau, cycle) / cycle).toFloat().coerceIn(0f, 1f)
    loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_ROTATE)?.takeIf { it != 0.0 }?.let { signed ->
        val cycle = abs(signed)
        effects += LayerAnimationVisualState(
            rotationDeltaDegrees = progressOf(cycle) * 360f * (if (signed < 0.0) -1f else 1f)
        )
    }
    loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_FLICKER)?.takeIf { it > 0.0 }?.let { cycle ->
        val t = (loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_FLICKER_T) ?: 0.5).coerceIn(0.0, 1.0)
        effects += LayerAnimationVisualState(alphaMultiplier = canvaFlickerOpacity(progressOf(cycle), cycle, t))
    }
    loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_PULSE)?.takeIf { it > 0.0 }?.let { cycle ->
        effects += LayerAnimationVisualState(scaleMultiplier = canvaPulseScale(progressOf(cycle)))
    }
    loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_WIGGLE)?.takeIf { it > 0.0 }?.let { cycle ->
        val t = (loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.STACK_WIGGLE_T) ?: 0.5).coerceIn(0.0, 1.0)
        val pose = canvaWigglePose(
            cycleProgress = progressOf(cycle),
            cycleMs = cycle,
            t = t,
            seed = loop.param(CanvaAnimationParams.SEED),
            width = width,
            height = height
        )
        effects += LayerAnimationVisualState(
            translationX = pose.translationX,
            translationY = pose.translationY,
            rotationDeltaDegrees = pose.rotationDegrees
        )
    }
    return effects
}

notes: Effects with authoredCurves=null are analytic formulas, verbatim from LayerAnimationVisualRuntime.kt (formula.kotlin = the LOOP / legacy branch).

canvaOneShot.kotlin is the ONE-SHOT branch from LayerAnimationCanvaRuntime.kt: Canva's intro tween while entering (p = raw progress) and outro tween while exiting (u = 1 - progress), returned WITHOUT the generic alpha x progress exit fade.
width/height are the LAYER size in px. intensity = spec.intensity clamped 0.1..4. vector = resolveAnimationVector(spec.direction). layerIndex = the layer's z-index in its page (0 = bottom).

Time bases: progress is eased AND ping-ponged (raised cosine) when infinite; cycleProgress is raw 0..1; pingPong is the raised-cosine mirror, NOT eased; ramp is the TRIANGULAR 0->1->0 mirror when infinite (Canva's continuous presets) and raw progress otherwise.
BREATHE/DRIFT/TECTONIC: one loop cycle is Canva's A -> B -> A ramp (LINEAR); DRIFT/TECTONIC amplitude = 120px x intensity; BREATHE A = 1 - .10 x intensity, B = 1 + .03 x intensity.

ROTATE/FLICKER/PULSE/WIGGLE: one cycle per durationMs. FLICKER: b = lerp(.6, .1, t), a = max(0, (cycle - 200) / 2); WIGGLE: Canva's rwf with n = floor(lerp(10, 100, t)), amp = lerp(.5, 1.8, t), g = cycle / (n + 1), r(s) = |cos(s) * seed| mod 1 (no seed: the layer's w * h); t = clamp(intensity - .5, 0, 1), the picker's intensity 1 = Canva's default t = .5.
A DEFAULT direction resolves to the type's preset direction; direction-aware reveals (RISE/SHIFT/PAN/SKATE) fall back to their own axis so they never go motionless.

Wipe masks carry an `edge` (LEFT default / RIGHT / TOP / BOTTOM) and `anchored`: the band grows from that edge; text renderers mirror LEFT/RIGHT for RTL text ONLY when anchored is false (Canva's WIPE / BASELINE / BLOCK set it), media never mirrors.

BLOCK (Canva's esf) adds an overlayBar channel: the layer's own box offset by (leftFraction, topFraction) of its size, clipped to the box, painted in params.barColor or the text colour; the text is hidden by an anchored Wipe at 0/1. ASCEND is per-WORD glyph motion. Both need a renderer that honours those channels.

params (docs/canva-animation-parity.md section 8.1) ride on each spec and are omitted when empty: a loop with params.concurrent = 1 is attached to the playback state and composed with the entrance/exit (alpha/scale multiply, translation/rotation/blur add); ramps r1*/r2* drive BREATHE/DRIFT/TECTONIC; stack* keys add repeating effects; unit/fill give FADE/BLUR/SUCCESSION/NEON Canva's writing styles through glyphMotion.canva (see runtime.canva.writingStyles).
Layer payload: animations{entrance,exit,loop}. Legacy single animation still migrates (infinite->loop, one-shot->entrance). A LOOP slot MUST be infinite=true.
